vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 31. Nay or No: 9. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 32 (80%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 51 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

For years, residents of Mountainside Community Cooperative in Camden relied on an aging sewer system that was at constant risk of failure. Sewage had to be trucked out several times a day, costing residents more than $100,000 annually.
 
Today, I visited Mountainside and met with the cooperative's president, Margaret Jones, and vice president, Maggie Adams, to discuss the vital improvements that have been made to the community's water and sewer infrastructure. It was wonderful to hear how these upgrades have improved the quality of life for residents.
 
In 2024, I secured more than $1.3 million through annual appropriations legislation to help connect Mountainside to Camden's municipal sewer system, replace aging water mains, and install new water meters and leak-detection equipment.
 
This is one of 83 water and wastewater projects across our state for which I’ve secured more than $164 million since 2021, because every Maine community deserves access to safe, reliable water and sewer infrastructure.

Three years ago, a horrific shooting in Lewiston claimed 18 innocent lives, injured more than a dozen others, and affected countless members of the greater Lewiston-Auburn community.
 
On this solemn anniversary, we remember those who were taken from us and stand with all those who still carry the scars from that devastating night.
 
In the years after, the people of our state have done what we always do: Law enforcement officers, first responders, health care workers, local leaders, community volunteers, and neighbors came together to support each other through unimaginable grief.
 
Since the shooting, I have worked with Lewiston to ensure the community has resources to help them heal and recover, including by strengthening mental health services and supporting the Maine Resiliency Center.
 
We will continue to remember the victims, support their families and loved ones, and stand with the people of this community.
 
Lewiston Strong.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
